insider_note: This is the 0-to-2π companion of the −π/2-to-π/2 integral of the same integrand — comparing the two shows how the reduction factor changes with the interval.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Reduce the range using the period property
steps.margin_note: First mark. Same even-even pattern — the range always collapses by a factor of 4.
steps.memory_tip: This is the sin²xcos⁴x version of the reduction that works whenever both powers are even.
steps.why: The same even-power reasoning applies: sin²x and cos⁴x are both even powers, so the integrand survives both reflections and the range collapses to 4 times the 0-to-π/2 integral.
common_mistakes: Re-deriving from scratch instead of using the reduction ∫₀^(2π) = 4∫₀^(π/2) that both even powers allow.
Losing a factor of 2 somewhere in the double reduction.

steps.label: Apply Walli's formula and evaluate
steps.margin_note: Second mark. 3/48 simplifies to 1/16 before the final multiplication.
steps.memory_tip: 4 × 1/16 × π/2 = π/8 — check each multiplication step separately.
steps.why: Walli's mixed-power formula for m=2, n=4 (both even) gives 3/48·π/2, and multiplying by the outer factor 4 gives π/8.
common_mistakes: Forgetting the outer factor 4 from the range reduction.
